phoenix-elixir.recommended_path: Fly is Phoenix's home turf. `fly launch` autodetects mix projects, builds a Dockerfile that bakes the BEAM release, and configures clustering via libcluster + DNS. Ideal for LiveView, Channels, presence — Fly's long-lived TCP + per-region affinity exactly matches the model.
caveats: Use the Fly-provided libcluster strategy for node discovery via 6PN private network.
Set release upgrades carefully — rolling deploys with multi-node clustering need erpc cookies in fly secrets.
Phoenix Postgres → Managed Postgres or legacy Fly Postgres in the same region as the app.

rails.recommended_path: `fly launch` detects Rails, generates a Dockerfile (or uses the Rails-provided one on Rails 7.1+), and provisions Postgres if the user opts in. Fly handles long-lived processes, ActionCable WebSockets, Sidekiq workers, and ActiveStorage well.
caveats: ActionCable + Redis: provision a Fly Redis (Upstash) or external; private-net URL is faster.
Sidekiq workers should run as a separate process_group with its own machines.
ActiveStorage: use Tigris for S3-compatible storage, or external S3.

django.recommended_path: Django + gunicorn/uvicorn deploy cleanly. `fly launch` autodetects manage.py and produces a Dockerfile. Pair with Managed Postgres in the same region. Channels (WebSockets) work because Fly machines are long-lived processes.
caveats: static files: collectstatic + WhiteNoise OR ship to Tigris.
Celery workers: separate machine group with the same Redis/RabbitMQ broker.
DEBUG=False in fly secrets (never in [env]).

flask.recommended_path: Flask + gunicorn deploys cleanly. `fly launch` produces a workable Dockerfile. Pair with Tigris (S3) and Managed Postgres if needed.
caveats: ProxyFix middleware: enable so Flask sees the real client IP from Fly's proxy.

fastapi.recommended_path: FastAPI + uvicorn or hypercorn — long-lived ASGI process matches Fly Machines. `fly launch` works.

express.recommended_path: Node + Express runs natively on Fly Machines. `fly launch` autodetects package.json, generates a Dockerfile.
caveats: If you depend on file-system caching, mount a volume.
WebSockets work — set min_machines_running to keep at least one process warm in each region.

fastify.recommended_path: Same shape as Express — Node + Fastify runs natively. `fly launch` produces a working baseline.
caveats: trustProxy: enable so the X-Forwarded-* headers are trusted from Fly's proxy.

nestjs.recommended_path: Larger Node app surface but maps onto Fly Machines cleanly. Microservices via Redis/TCP work because the private network supports them.
caveats: Microservices over TCP: use the 6PN private network address (<app>.internal) for inter-app calls.
TypeORM / Prisma: pair with Managed Postgres in the same region.

nextjs.recommended_path: `fly launch` detects Next and produces a Node-runtime Dockerfile (standalone output). Server-rendered routes, server actions, ISR all work because machines are long-lived.
caveats: Use Next.js standalone output (output: 'standalone' in next.config.js) for the smallest image.
ISR cache lives on disk — mount a volume if you want it to survive deploys.
next/image: use the default loader; Fly's network handles the bandwidth fine.
dependencies_to_flag: sharp (works), node:fs (works on Fly unlike serverless)

hono.recommended_path: Hono is Workers-first; on Fly it runs via the Node adapter (long-lived process). Works, but you're paying for Fly's machine model where Workers' ms-billing might be cheaper. Verdict: partial — pick Fly if you also want websockets/long-lived TCP/volumes; pick Cloudflare Workers otherwise.
caveats: Hono's edge runtime features (cf bindings) won't apply on Fly — strip @cloudflare/* deps.

spring-boot.recommended_path: JVM apps run cleanly on Fly Machines. Build a JLink image or use Eclipse Temurin base. Pair with Managed Postgres.
caveats: Tune -Xmx to the machine's memory_mb minus overhead (~20%).
First request after deploy is slow due to JIT — set min_machines_running >= 1 for prod.

dotnet.recommended_path: ASP.NET Core runs natively on Fly Machines via the .NET runtime base image. `fly launch` recognizes .csproj.
caveats: DataProtection keys: persist to a mounted volume or Redis to avoid cookie invalidation across machines.

go-monolith.recommended_path: Go services compile to a single static binary; Dockerfile is trivial (FROM scratch / FROM alpine). Excellent fit for Fly — fast cold start, low memory, native long-lived TCP.

rust.recommended_path: Rust services compile to single static binary. Excellent fit. axum / actix / hyper all work cleanly on Fly Machines.

deno.recommended_path: Deno runtime in a Dockerfile (denoland/deno:alpine base). Long-lived HTTP fits. WebSockets work.
caveats: Deno KV is Deno-Deploy-only — pick Postgres / Redis / Tigris for state.

bun.recommended_path: Bun runtime in a Dockerfile (oven/bun base). Long-lived process model. Bun's HTTP server is fast.
caveats: Bun is still maturing — pin the bun version in the Dockerfile.

websocket-heavy.recommended_path: Fly's machine model is built for long-lived processes — WebSockets, SSE, gRPC streaming all work natively. min_machines_running >= 1 keeps at least one warm.
caveats: session affinity: HTTP service has sticky sessions via fly-replay header; for chat/presence put state in Redis/Postgres so any machine can serve.

ml-gpu.recommended_path: Fly Machines GPU (A10, L40S, A100, H100) for inference and training. Bill on duration. Pair with R2/Tigris for model artifacts.
caveats: GPU machines are expensive — set auto_stop_machines='stop' aggressively, or use min_machines_running=0 with a slower cold start.
Image: must use the CUDA-compatible base; build context can grow large.

static-spa.recommended_path: Don't pay for a Machine to serve static files. Use Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, Vercel, or another static host. Fly.io's value is long-lived processes.

hugo.recommended_path: Static site generators belong on a CDN host (Pages / Netlify / Vercel), not Fly Machines.

wordpress.recommended_path: PHP-FPM + nginx in a Dockerfile runs on Fly Machines, but the wp-content/uploads tree needs careful planning: mount a Fly volume (single-region; not multi-writer) OR offload to Tigris/S3 via wp-stateless. Multi-region WP is non-trivial; pick a single primary region and serve elsewhere via cache.
caveats: wp-cron via system cron + ?doing_wp_cron disabled.
Multi-machine WP needs object cache (Redis) and shared media (S3/Tigris) — ad-hoc setups break.
Backup: snapshot the volume daily; export DB via `wp db export` to Tigris.

laravel.recommended_path: PHP + nginx + Octane (or php-fpm) on Fly Machines. `fly launch` autodetects artisan. Queue workers + scheduler in separate process_groups.
caveats: trust the proxy: TrustProxies middleware with TRUSTED_PROXIES='*' (or the Fly proxy CIDR).
queues: Horizon-on-Fly works; Redis goes via the private network.
storage: S3-compat Tigris or external.

mysql-app.recommended_path: Fly doesn't offer Managed MySQL. Run MySQL yourself on a Fly Machine + volume (single primary; replicas non-trivial), or use external (PlanetScale, RDS, etc.).
caveats: Self-hosted MySQL on a single volume = single point of failure. Take snapshots; consider external for prod.

postgres-app.recommended_path: Use Fly Managed Postgres (newer offering) or legacy Fly Postgres (an app you operate). Same-region as your app for low latency.
caveats: Legacy Fly Postgres: you operate it. Set up replicas + snapshot retention. Rotate passwords with `fly pg revoke`.
Managed Postgres: simpler, billed per-cluster. Less knob-twisting.

mongodb-app.recommended_path: Fly doesn't offer Managed MongoDB. Run MongoDB yourself on a Fly Machine + volume (replica set requires multiple machines + careful coordination), or use MongoDB Atlas (most apps choose this).
caveats: MongoDB replica set on Fly: every member needs static private IP and persistent volume; it's doable but operationally heavy.
MongoDB Atlas: use the connection string via fly secrets. Latency depends on Atlas region.

redis-app.recommended_path: Use Fly's Upstash-on-Fly Redis (`fly redis create`). TLS by default, private-net URL. Or run your own Redis on a Machine + volume.
caveats: Upstash-on-Fly is the easy path — $X/mo per database, no operational overhead.
Self-managed Redis: pin to a region; use AOF + RDB; snapshot the volume.

s3-storage.recommended_path: Tigris is Fly's S3-compatible offering, baked into orgs. `fly storage create`. Free egress within Fly. Migrate from S3 with `aws s3 sync ... --endpoint-url=https://fly.storage.tigris.dev`.
caveats: Tigris is global by default — read-after-write within the same region is strong; cross-region is eventually consistent.
Public buckets: configure CORS for browser uploads.

long-running-compute.recommended_path: Fly Machines run for as long as you need them. Long-running CPU compute is the normal model. For batch / GPU workloads, Machines GPU (auto-stop after the job).
caveats: Set restart_policy=no for one-shot jobs (machines exit and stay exited).
Use auto_destroy=true for ephemeral compute machines.

media-processing-heavy.recommended_path: FFmpeg / ImageMagick / sharp / headless browsers run inside the Dockerfile. Pair with Tigris for input/output. GPU machines for ML-heavy media (Whisper, Stable Diffusion).
caveats: Build context: keep the Dockerfile slim; use multi-stage so the runtime layer doesn't ship the build toolchain.
Disk: mount a volume for scratch space if jobs are large.

elixir.recommended_path: Same as phoenix-elixir — Fly is the BEAM's natural home: clustering via 6PN, fly_clustering or libcluster.DNS, hot reloads via mix release.
